title: A Ledger for the Bridge
premise: In the waning months of a colonial border war, Coral Okafor, a battlefield nurse, secretly records in her ledger the names of soldiers officially listed as missing or erased — men whose deaths would embarrass their officers. When a stranger named Elias Vann arrives at her field hospital carrying a letter in the unmistakable handwriting of Captain Rowan Ashe, a man officially dead for two years, Coral realizes the ledger she keeps may be the only proof that Ashe survived and that his 'death' was arranged to bury a massacre. Together they must smuggle the ledger and Ashe's letter past three military checkpoints to a tribunal journalist in the port city, pursued by Major Halloway's men who will burn anything that remembers. The book ends at the third checkpoint, where Coral chooses to surrender herself as a diversion so the ledger reaches print — and in the final chapter, months later, she reads her own name among those the tribunal restores.
about_author: Vesper Almeida is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed letters from forgotten wars. They write historical fiction about the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: What the Orders Weigh
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. In a flooded field hospital near the river bridge, Coral triages wounded soldiers while quietly recording in her ledger the names officers omit from their reports. The chapter establishes her ritual of memory and the war's casual erasures. Emotional beat: weary resolve — she measures her days in what can be carried when evacuation orders come.

chapters.title: The Stranger at the Tent Flap
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A mud-caked stranger, Elias Vann, collapses at the hospital claiming to be a civilian courier. He carries a bloodstained letter addressed to no one and everyone — written in the hand of Captain Rowan Ashe, declared dead two years ago. Coral recognizes the handwriting because Ashe once wrote to thank her for tending his men. Beat: disbelief sharpening into dread.

chapters.title: A Hand That Should Be Dust
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Flashback woven through present: how Elias received the letter from a dying deserter in the marshes, and what it claims — that Ashe lives, imprisoned, and that his 'death' covered a massacre at Kessel Ford. Elias doesn't know if he believes it; he only knows men are hunting him. Beat: fear tempered by stubborn obligation.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At night Coral compares the letter against her own ledger and finds the dates align: every name missing from official reports matches the men supposedly lost at Kessel Ford. She realizes her private record is now evidence. Beat: the quiet terror of a secret becoming dangerous.

chapters.title: Major Halloway Comes to Count
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Major Halloway inspects the hospital, charming and precise, asking pointed questions about deserters on the river road. Coral lies smoothly for the first time in her life and hates how easily it comes. Beat: the first direct collision between loyalty to her patients and loyalty to truth.

chapters.title: Elias Tells the Truth Badly
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Under pressure from Coral, Elias admits he isn't a courier but Ashe's former clerk, dismissed after questioning the Kessel Ford reports. He came looking for someone who kept records; he'd heard rumors of a nurse who wrote down names. Beat: shame transmuted into partnership as Coral agrees to help.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints Between Here and Print
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral maps the route to the port city where tribunal journalist Adaeze Brandt is gathering testimony: the bridge checkpoint, the quarry pass, and the customs house. Each requires papers they don't have. Beat: cold planning replacing panic; the mission takes shape.

chapters.title: The Nurse Who Keeps Two Books
chapters.summary: Sister Imelda's POV. The head nurse, a devout pragmatist, discovers Coral's ledger and must choose between reporting her and covering for her. Imelda has spent thirty years obeying rules that never saved anyone. Beat: an unexpected ally born of quiet disillusionment.

chapters.title: Leaving the Wounded Behind
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. An evacuation order forces Coral to choose: leave with the wounded convoy and abandon the mission, or slip away during the chaos. She entrusts her sickest patient to Imelda and walks into the rain with the ledger sewn into her coat. Beat: guilt as the price of conviction.

chapters.title: The Bridge at Dusk
chapters.summary: Shared POV. First checkpoint: the river bridge, where sentries search carts for deserters. Elias poses a corpse-hauler moving bodies for burial; Coral rides in the cart among the shrouded dead, ledger beneath her heart. A sergeant nearly lifts the shroud over her. Beat: claustrophobic suspense, held breath.

chapters.title: Names in the Mud
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. On the far bank, Elias confesses more: the deserter who gave him the letter was his brother. Grief loosens something between him and Coral, who tells him why she started the ledger — a boy she couldn't save whose name no report ever carried. Beat: intimacy forged in shared mourning.

chapters.title: Hounds on the Quarry Road
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Halloway's riders reach the hospital, and Imelda sends a warning via a wounded driver. Coral and Elias cut cross-country toward the quarry pass as pursuit tightens. Beat: flight, adrenaline, and the growing sense that Halloway knows exactly who he's hunting.

chapters.title: The Quarry Pass
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Second checkpoint: a stone chokepoint manned by conscripts barely older than her patients. Coral gambles on mercy, telling a young corporal the truth — not all of it, just enough. He looks away while they pass. Beat: fragile faith that ordinary men still have consciences.

chapters.title: What Halloway Keeps in His Trunk
chapters.summary: Halloway's POV. Interlude inside the antagonist: Halloway reviews the Kessel Ford file, revealing he didn't order the massacre but falsified the reports afterward to protect his patron, General Verey. He burns a copy of Ashe's letter recovered from the marsh. Beat: chilling ordinariness — a man managing paperwork, not evil, worse.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgot Its Dead
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Sheltering in a river town, Coral finds a memorial wall with Kessel Ford's casualties listed as 'died of fever' — the lie already carved in stone. She understands the stakes: the ledger isn't just evidence, it's a counter-monument. Beat: righteous anger hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Ferry Inn
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A sympathetic innkeeper offers help, then sells them out to Halloway's men for his sons' safety. Elias is captured covering Coral's escape through the fen; the ledger stays with her. Beat: betrayal, sacrifice, and Coral's agonizing choice to run rather than surrender both of them.

chapters.title: Alone With the Names
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Hidden in a drainage culvert, Coral debates destroying the ledger to save herself and Elias. She reads the names aloud instead, one by one, and cannot. Beat: the thematic crux — memory as a debt that can't be defaulted on.

chapters.title: The Customs House
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Third checkpoint: the port customs house, now crawling with Halloway's officers expecting them. Coral walks in openly, posing as a nurse escorting a prisoner — Elias, bruised but alive, traded back to her in a desperate bribe using Imelda's contraband medicine. Beat: audacity as camouflage; tension at its peak.

chapters.title: Everything Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Cornered at the dock with the tribune's office in sight, Coral creates a diversion — announcing herself as the witness Halloway fears, letting herself be arrested so the guards chase her while Elias runs the ledger to Adaeze Brandt. Beat: climax; the ultimate inversion of her instinct to hide.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Halloway interrogates Coral personally, offering her freedom for the ledger's location. She tells him the truth: it's already beyond his reach, and every name in it is a sentence he'll serve. His composure cracks for the first time. Beat: moral victory inside physical defeat.

chapters.title: The Tribunal Reads Aloud
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Brandt publishes the ledger; the Kessel Ford testimony detonates across the capital. Ashe is found alive in a military prison; Halloway is arrested, Verey protected but exposed. Imelda reads the names to her ward. Elias stands at the prison gate waiting. Beat: catharsis — truth arriving late but arriving.

chapters.title: A Ledger With Room Left
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Months later, released under amnesty, Coral visits the new memorial where the real names are being recut into stone. She starts a second ledger — this time of the living, the restored, the returned. Beat: resolution; memory transformed from grief into guardianship.
